intervals.quote: The SABRE experiment aims to shed light on this controversy by detecting the annual modulation in the same target material as DAMA with twin detectors at LNGS in Italy and at SUPL in Australia.

name: SABRE Collaboration
notes: Two sites: LNGS (SABRE North) and SUPL (SABRE South); the 2024 talk names separate SABRE North and SABRE South Collaborations under one project. No roster or member count was found; the Atlas records no memberships.

summary.plain: The international team behind SABRE, a pair of sodium-iodide dark matter detectors, one in Italy and one in Australia, built to test the yearly signal reported by DAMA with even cleaner crystals. Placing detectors in both hemispheres helps separate a true dark matter signal from seasonal effects.
summary.technical: SABRE (Sodium-iodide with Active Background REjection): two detectors, SABRE North at LNGS (INFN, Princeton and others) and SABRE South at SUPL (Australian institutions of the ARC Centre of Excellence for Dark Matter Particle Physics), sharing crystal R&D; the 2024 talk is given 'on behalf of SABRE North and SABRE South Collaborations'. SABRE North spokesperson: Aldo Ianni (2026 slides).
